name: Miami
title: Holidays in Miami
intro: Turquoise sea, airboats in the Everglades and Cuban food in Little Havana. Here's what Miami is like with the family, when to go and how long to stay.
facts_note: Check entry rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: November to April is warm, dry and sunny, which makes it a winter sun favourite. Summer is hot and humid with afternoon storms. Hurricane season runs from June to November, peaking in September.

things.name: South Beach
things.blurb: Wide white sand, lifeguard huts and pastel art deco hotels.

things.name: Everglades airboat
things.blurb: Skim across the grasslands looking for alligators, about an hour away.

things.name: Frost Science Museum
things.blurb: An aquarium you can look up into, plus a planetarium.

things.name: Zoo Miami
things.blurb: A big open zoo where the animals suit the heat.

things.name: Crandon Park
things.blurb: A calmer family beach on Key Biscayne. You pay to park.

things.name: Little Havana
things.blurb: Cuban music, domino players and great sandwiches.

faqs.question: Is Miami good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes, as a beach and city mix, or as the start of a Florida Keys road trip. South Beach is lively at night, so families often prefer Key Biscayne or Sunny Isles.

faqs.question: How many nights do you need?
faqs.answer: Five to seven nights, or add Orlando or the Keys for two weeks.

faqs.question: Do UK families need a visa?
faqs.answer: Most British passport holders, children included, apply for an ESTA online before they fly rather than a visa. Check GOV.UK for the current rules.

faqs.question: Can you drive to the Florida Keys?
faqs.answer: Yes, the Overseas Highway runs over the sea to Key West, about four hours each way. It's best with a night or two on the way.
